title: End-to-End Commerce Publishing and Runtime
readerIntent: Follow approved commerce data from authoring to a customer request.
owner: Composed commerce capabilities; each retains its authority
summary: Authoring publishes exact approved Product, Price, Stock, Store, and content forms to Online; checkout then composes Cart, Inventory, Payment, Order, and Fulfillment without merging their authority.

sections.heading: Authoring and publishing
items: Business users update staged content, products, prices, stores, or inventory under their owning schemas.
A workflow carrier associates exact changed items and versions.
Manual and automatic actions validate dependencies and obtain approval.
nPublish calls each domain adapter and authenticated Online target transport.
Online persistence succeeds before cache invalidation, search indexing, and publication events complete or reconcile.

sections.heading: Prepare a realistic example
items: Create one tenant and enterprise with Apparel and Electronics Storefront Sites, separate CMS and product catalogs, their Stores, countries, channels, currencies, and eligible warehouses.
Create an iPhone product and variant, a UAE price list and scoped prices, warehouse balances, service zones, normalized units, and the relationships needed for the Electronics website.
Keep secrets and environment endpoints in runtime configuration, not content data. Use stable business codes for references and let import resolve database identifiers.
Before publication, verify ownership, required relationships, version compatibility, price dates and currency, unit compatibility, stock policy, and the exact item versions carried by the workflow.

sections.heading: Customer request
items: Customer opens apparel.nodics.com.
Storefront resolves the Site, Apparel Store, tenant, enterprise, country, channel, locale, currency, and catalog handles.
CMS supplies the Apparel content/page model directly.
Product supplies the selected catalog product and variant.
Pricing resolves the applicable contextual price.
Inventory sources eligible warehouses and returns on-hand, reserved, and available-to-sell according to the safe contract.
Each module verifies context and authorization; BackOffice and Storefront are not data-plane proxies.

sections.heading: Checkout, payment, and fulfillment
items: Cart and Order share the same commercial structure at different lifecycle stages. Cart owns pre-order intent; Order owns the immutable order projection created through checkout placement.

Line entries, delivery groups, delivery allocations, payment groups, and payment allocations are first-class submodels so one item quantity can be split across addresses, warehouses, carriers, and payment methods.

Payment separates business methods from provider adapters. Card, Cash on Delivery, Wallet, Advance, Offline, or customer methods are enterprise-scoped payment methods; CyberSource, Stripe, PayPal, bank, wallet, deferred, or manual handlers are payment providers selected by policy.

Fulfillment separates shipping modes from carrier providers. Standard, Express, Pickup, Local Delivery, or customer modes are business delivery choices; carrier, aggregator, pickup-network, or local-delivery providers execute labels, tracking, and handoff through adapters.

Inventory owns stock, reservations, allocations, transfers, sourcing, pre-order, backorder, and overbooking policy. Checkout may request holds and allocation evidence, but it does not mutate stock directly.
Promotion remains a later strategy layer. Checkout data structures keep discounts and tax evidence separable so promotions can be added without changing the allocation model.

sections.heading: Distributed delivery and payment example
items: A cart has one product entry with quantity `3`. Checkout may split that entry into two delivery allocations: quantity `2` to Address A and quantity `1` to Address B.
The same entry can be split into payment allocations: quantity `2` or its calculated amount authorized by Card, and quantity `1` deferred to Cash on Delivery or another configured method.

Each allocated quantity can later attach inventory allocation evidence. Where a business requires serial-number tracking, the customer module extends the allocation evidence to point to serialized inventory records without bypassing Inventory.

If available stock is insufficient, Inventory policy decides whether reservation should fail, use backorder, use pre-order capacity, or accept allowed overbooking with an advance-payment requirement. Payment collects only the governed amount and method selected by checkout policy.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Two websites and catalogs under one tenant/enterprise.
Context spoofing, wrong audience, inactive Store/Site, and cross-tenant denial.
Missing/ambiguous product, price, stock, unit conversion, and warehouse scope.
Split delivery and split payment for one line item and for partial quantity of the same line item.
Provider outage, retry, reconciliation, overbooking limits, advance-charge requirements, idempotency replay, and duplicate fulfillment/payment command prevention.
Staged approval, target outage, partial derived refresh, retry, reconciliation, rollback, cache/search consistency, load, security, and regression.

sections.heading: Failure and recovery walkthrough
items: If approval fails, nothing is published and the workflow retains actionable validation evidence. If the Online target rejects the request, retry uses the same publication identity so it cannot create a duplicate.

If authoritative persistence succeeds but search indexing or cache invalidation fails, record a recoverable derived-state failure and reconcile it; do not roll back silently or claim that the old projection is authoritative.

During a customer request, a missing optional recommendation may degrade safely, while an untrusted context, ambiguous price, incompatible unit, or uncertain stock commitment must fail according to the owning contract.

Complete acceptance records positive, negative, boundary, contract, integration, security, performance, observability, recovery, and regression results for every module boundary rather than testing only the final page.

sections.heading: Axis and BackOffice exposure
items: Axis groups commerce authoring and operations from backend BackOffice navigation metadata. Catalog focuses on product/categorization/enrichment/publishing records; Commerce Operations groups pricing, stock, stores, carts, orders, payment, and fulfillment.

Reusable Axis workbench components provide search, query builder, configurable sortable grids, export, create/update where authorized, and reusable schema detail panels. Business-specific views are layered later when they add value.

Lifecycle actions are backend metadata. Axis can display Payment retry/reconciliation and Fulfillment label/dispatch/return actions as planned or executable depending on whether the owning module exposes an operation route.
Disabled or planned items such as Tax Records, Fraud Checks, Promotions, and Coupons must stay visibly planned or hidden until an owning backend capability exists.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
items: Customer projects customize commerce through later project modules: extend schemas, permissions, validation, import/export data, publication adapters, and BackOffice metadata without editing framework modules.
Do not build an Axis-only commerce control plane or duplicate Product, Pricing, Inventory, Store, Cart, Order, Units, CMS, or nMedia state. Axis is an experience client over backend-owned contracts.

Verify end-to-end customizations with module contract tests, BackOffice bootstrap/navigation tests, route-scoped Axis tests, import/export checks, permission filtering, publication/recovery tests, and rollback procedures for the customer layer.
